Answer: B
Reason: The ultrasound images demonstrate a hyperechoic mass with cystic spaces in the fetal thorax (indicated by arrows) that is exerting mass effect, which is characteristic of a congenital pulmonary airway malformation (CPAM) typically located in the middle or lower lobes; this mass effect commonly displaces the mediastinum/heart to the contralateral side and can elevate the ipsilateral hemidiaphragm.
